editorial_lock: November 9 user-established order; do not reorder
stats_status: 20 of 20 candidates have sourced PPG/RPG/APG; individual stats still need final source/date reconciliation, including Cameron Boozer's 16.4 vs 16.2 PPG conflict. Previous award movements and official injury designations not finalized.

mvp_watch.name: Luka Dončić
mvp_watch.analysis: The league's most explosive scoring engine is still our standard. His 32-point, 10-assist outing against Atlanta underlined how his playmaking survives even when the jumper is not automatic.

mvp_watch.name: Victor Wembanyama
mvp_watch.analysis: The strongest two-way counterargument to Luka: 40 points and nine blocks against Phoenix, changing both the scoreboard and the shots opponents dare attempt.

mvp_watch.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
mvp_watch.analysis: His control of Oklahoma City's offense and ability to manufacture efficient looks keep him in the top tier. The Thunder's team success strengthens the case.

mvp_watch.name: Jayson Tatum
mvp_watch.analysis: Tatum's position reflects his established value as a primary creator and two-way wing. We need to weigh current availability and team results without inventing a stat line.

mvp_watch.name: Stephen Curry
mvp_watch.analysis: Golden State's offense still bends around his shooting gravity. His impact goes beyond points: defenses compromise their shape simply to deny him touches.

mvp_watch.name: Cade Cunningham
mvp_watch.analysis: Detroit's rise gives Cade a compelling leadership case. The test is whether his creation remains steady when opponents force the ball out of his hands.

mvp_watch.name: Tyrese Maxey
mvp_watch.analysis: Philadelphia's pace and offensive organization run through Maxey. His speed turns defensive hesitation into immediate pressure on the rim.

mvp_watch.name: Nikola Jokić
mvp_watch.analysis: Denver's fulcrum remains the standard for decision-making bigs. We will distinguish his all-around impact from the Nuggets' early record.

mvp_watch.name: Alperen Şengün
mvp_watch.analysis: Houston's inside-out creation gives the Rockets a second offensive language. His passing from the middle of the floor unlocks the surrounding talent.

mvp_watch.name: Ty Jerome
mvp_watch.analysis: Memphis's early success puts Jerome's shot-making and decision-making in focus. His November 9 scoring performance against Toronto supports the case.

rookie_watch.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
rookie_watch.analysis: Our No. 1 rookie has earned the spotlight through his two-way energy and growing role with Golden State. The next step is proving the production holds across different matchups.

rookie_watch.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
rookie_watch.analysis: Acuff's placement reflects his creation burden and offensive upside. We will measure his efficiency and turnover control alongside his scoring.

rookie_watch.name: Cameron Boozer
rookie_watch.analysis: Boozer's rebounding, playmaking and physical maturity make this a real three-player race at the top. Memphis's winning start adds context.

rookie_watch.name: Caleb Wilson
rookie_watch.analysis: Wilson has to create value in a difficult Chicago environment. His production should be judged on responsibility as well as raw totals.

rookie_watch.name: AJ Dybantsa
rookie_watch.analysis: Dybantsa's ceiling remains enormous, but availability and minutes must be documented before the next edition goes live.

rookie_watch.name: Darryn Peterson
rookie_watch.analysis: Peterson's scoring talent gives Utah a reason to watch every possession. We need the current efficiency and usage before making stronger statistical claims.

rookie_watch.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
rookie_watch.analysis: Brown's placement recognizes the flashes of shot creation. Consistency and role clarity are the next checkpoints.

rookie_watch.name: Brayden Burries
rookie_watch.analysis: Burries has the tools to contribute as a perimeter scorer. His shot selection and defensive discipline matter as much as his highlights.

rookie_watch.name: Meleek Thomas
rookie_watch.analysis: Thomas has an opportunity to make a meaningful impression in Minnesota's rotation. We will track his role alongside the team's injury situation.

rookie_watch.name: Aday Mara
rookie_watch.analysis: Mara rounds out the locked ten. His size and interior skill give him a distinct developmental path; playing time and availability need verification.

publication_guard: Do not publish until full current season averages, previous rank, team and injury checks complete.
